newsitem.title: USA: Strong dollar in U.S. interest, says Rubin.
newsitem.headline: Strong dollar in U.S. interest, says Rubin.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin Thursday reiterated his support for a strong dollar, saying it helped keep inflation down and interest rates low.

"A strong dollar is very much in our nation's interest," Rubin said in an interview on Nightly Business Report to be aired later today on Public Television, adding. "with a strong dollar you have lower interest rates and you have lower inflation."
U.S. carmakers have complained that the strong U.S. currency -- it jumped to a 33-month high against the yen this week -- has hurt their ability to compete overseas.
Rubin argued, however, that U.S. carmakers were the most competitive in the world and repeated his opposition to using the dollar as a weapon to increase exports.
"A strong dollar has played a real role in the economic prosperity we've had over the last four years," he said.
Rubin saw continued solid U.S. economic growth and low inflation in the period ahead although he declined to look at it on a quarter by quarter basis.

In the interview that was shown on Reuters Financial Television, Rubin also said he believed that the Japanese economy was on the right track although it was important for the authorities to continue to pursue policies to keep the economy moving.
"It is extremely important that they maintain the right mix of fiscal and monetary policies to continue to have strong growth generated by domestic demand," he said.
Japan is slated to raise consumption taxes next year but Rubin said this should only be done if the overall economy is strong enough to accomodate it without weakening.
"That should only take place if it looks like growth momentum is sufficient so it can be accomodated without reducing growth," he said.
Asked whether he expected to remain in any future Clinton administration should the president win on Nov 5, Rubin declined to comment saying he was concentrating on the election.
